The Illinois Senate is the ___E:upper chamber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_house)___ of the ___E:Illinois General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_General_Assembly)___ , the ___E:legislative branch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislative_branch)___ of the government of the ___E:State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state)___ of ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ in the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ .

The body was created by the first state constitution adopted in 1818. Under the ___E:Illinois Constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Illinois)___ of 1970, the Illinois Senate is made up of 59 ___E:senators U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_senator)___ elected from individual legislative districts determined by population and redistricted every 10 years; based on the 2020 ___E:U.S. census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._census)___ each senator represents approximately 213,347 people.

Senate districts are divided into three groups, each group having a two-year term at a different part of the decade between censuses, with the rest of the decade being taken up by two four-year terms.

For example, group one elects senators for terms of four years, four years and two years, group two elects senators for terms of four years, two years and four years, and group three elects senators for terms of two years, four years and four years.
This ensures that the Senate reflects changes made when the General Assembly redistricts itself after each census.
Usually, depending on the election year, roughly one-third or two-thirds of Senate seats are contested.
On rare occasions (usually after a census), all Senate seats are up for election.

In contrast, the ___E:Illinois House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_House_of_Representatives)___ is made up of 118 members with its entire membership elected to two-year terms.
House districts are formed by dividing each Senate district in half,  with each senator having two " ___E:associated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nesting_(voting_districts))___ " representatives.

The Illinois Senate convenes at the ___E:Illinois State Capitol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Capitol)___ in ___E:Springfield, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Illinois)___ .

Its first official working day is the second Wednesday of January each year. Its primary duties are to pass bills into law, approve the state budget, confirm appointments to state departments and agencies, act on federal constitutional amendments and propose constitutional amendments for Illinois.

It also has the power to override gubernatorial vetoes through a three-fifths majority vote. The Illinois Senate tries impeachments made by the House of Representatives, and can convict impeached officers by a two-thirds vote.
Voting in the Illinois Senate is done by members pushing one of three buttons.
Unlike most states, the Illinois Senate allows members to vote yes, no, or present.
It takes 30 affirmative votes to pass legislation during final action.
The number of negative votes does not matter.

Therefore, voting present has the same effect on the tally as voting no. ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ began his political career in the Illinois Senate before going on to become President of the United States.
